sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at a 20.5% CAGR to $155.2 billion, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% on Microsoft Cloud growth and Azure [D472][P17].
FY2018 broke the net-income line, falling 35.0% on the TCJA charge, while FY2019 rebounded 136.8% on a $2.6 billion intangible-transfer tax benefit [D48][D101][P61].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth [D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, as Azure and other cloud services grew 41% on demand across workloads [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 [D649][P14].
Incremental operating margin was 53.3% in FY2026, with revenue growth outpacing operating-cost growth by 10.3pp [D498][D499].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3%, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue grew 21.1% against revenue growth of 17.8% [F30][D486][D981][D489][D472].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue, a window low, and selling and marketing to 8.0%, so operating margin still rose 1.2pp [D450][D985][D451][D487].
Net margin jumped 4.2pp to 40.3% partly on $6.5 billion of OpenAI investment gains in other income [F70][D488][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, on higher customer cash receipts and lower income-tax payments [D477][F100][P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion, a 34.9% capex-to-revenue ratio [D478][F120][D479][F110][D455].
Free cash flow was 0.50x net income, a window low against a 0.91x median, and 20.2% of revenue versus a 30.3% median [D460][D988][D990][D456][D984].
Capex ran at 3.38x D&A, and stock-based compensation was 6.8% of operating cash flow [D461][D462].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion, but the current ratio of 1.23x is a window low [D495][D464][F200][D991].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
Return on average equity of 34.0% sits at the peer median of 38.8% [D471][D1010][D1011].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026 [R1][D406][D460].
The gap is capex-led: investing outflow reached $139.5 billion, driven by a $51.4 billion rise in property and equipment additions [F130][P1].
This is a deliberate AI build-out rather than an earnings-quality problem, but it leaves free cash flow margin at a window low [D982].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, so FY2017 comparisons use first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
Capex at 34.9% of revenue: a move back toward the FY2025 level of 22.9% would lift free cash flow margin above its 20.2% low [D455][D401][D456].
Operating margin at 46.8%: holding above the 41.7% median confirms the leverage trend, while a drop below it would reverse it [F50][D975].
Intelligent Cloud margin at 41.3%, down from 44.3% in FY2021: further decline would signal AI infrastructure costs outrunning Azure growth [D963][D958].
